skill.name: incidentio-cli
skill.description: Use the incidentio CLI to query and manage incident.io incidents, alerts, schedules, catalogs, workflows, and status pages.
skill.summary: CLI guidance for incident.io public APIs and authenticated internal dashboard endpoints.
skill.author: paymog

security_audit.summary: All 207 static findings are false positives for their reported patterns, including Markdown backticks, service resource IDs, and intended authentication references. Two semantic findings identify credential exposure through command arguments and unsafe write-request probing. No evidence found of prompt injection or malicious exfiltration; only SKILL.md was available, so CLI implementation behavior was not verified.

remediation.issue: Credential examples place API keys, session cookies, and secret values in process arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer protected secret injection, supported stdin import, or restricted body files. Warn against literal secrets in command arguments, shell history, transcripts, and logs.

remediation.issue: Endpoint discovery uses authenticated write probes without an isolated test environment.
remediation.suggestion: Require a sandbox organization and explicit approval before write probes. Prefer documentation or read-only discovery, then verify changes and cleanup.

content.user_title: Manage incident.io Operations Through the CLI
content.value_statement: Incident response work spans incidents, alerts, schedules, catalogs, and status pages. This skill provides CLI commands and recipes for incident.io public APIs and internal dashboard endpoints.
actual_capabilities: Discover resource commands and query incidents with bracket filters, date ranges, and cursor pagination.
Create incidents and manage actions, follow-ups, alerts, escalations, and on-call schedules.
Create catalog entries with relationships and configure catalog-backed custom fields.
Manage status pages, components, layouts, subscribers, and retrospective incident records.
Configure alert route bindings, navigation expressions, workflows, and incident policies.
Use scoped Bearer authentication or imported browser sessions for public and internal endpoints.
limitations: Requires an installed incidentio binary, network access, and valid incident.io credentials.
Internal dashboard commands require an imported browser session and can change without public API guarantees.
Available actions depend on credential permissions, organization configuration, and subscription limits.
Contains instructions rather than bundled CLI implementation; several examples require real resource IDs and complete request bodies.

best_practices: Use least-privilege credentials and keep API keys, session cookies, and secret values out of command logs and shared transcripts.
Read current resource state and verify organization, permissions, and route versions before approving writes.
Use a sandbox organization for endpoint discovery and experimental internal API requests.
anti_patterns: Pasting live credentials or browser sessions into chat, inline command arguments, or shared logs.
Using production write requests as harmless endpoint discovery probes.
Applying example IDs, stale route versions, or destructive commands without checking targets and obtaining approval.

faq.question: What must be installed before using this skill?
faq.answer: The incidentio CLI must already be installed. You also need network access and credentials for your incident.io organization.

faq.question: Can an API key run every command?
faq.answer: No. Public commands use scoped Bearer keys. Internal dashboard commands require an imported authenticated browser session.

faq.question: Can it create public status pages?
faq.answer: The documented internal commands create pages, components, and layouts. They require a browser session and remain subject to subscription limits.

faq.question: Does the skill include the CLI implementation?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains only SKILL.md instructions. The CLI implementation and its credential handling were not independently verified.

faq.question: Why do alert route updates need the current version?
faq.answer: The documented internal API uses optimistic concurrency. Read the current version, increment it, and omit incompatible users fields from escalation targets.

faq.question: How should unknown internal endpoints be tested?
faq.answer: Use an isolated test organization and obtain approval before write requests. Partial request bodies can still cause changes if an endpoint accepts them.
